# dsh-compaction-continuum
English | 简体中文
A context-compaction backend for DeepSeek Harness, maintained by 2718Labs. The project name is Struc
tural Compression (结构性压缩).
The compaction backend shipped with Harness asks a model to read the history and write a summary, wh
ich is then written back into the context. This plugin takes a different route: it extracts items wi
th verbatim citations from the source, computes the load-bearing relations between them, and keeps o
nly the items that are load-bearing and verifiable against the source. The compression ratio is comp
arable to the shipped backend; the difference is that the published content is traceable.
## Measured results (plugin installed)
The figures below were measured after installing this plugin; the object of measurement is the plugi
n, not the shipped backend.
Precondition: the self-test reports `backendUsesHookedSummarize: true`, meaning the preset-plane shi
pped engine instance is already running this compressor.
| Observation | Measured value |

| Backend | shipped `BasicCompactionEngine` instance with `summarize` replaced |
| Replayed span | 3

66 messages (system + 365 shadowed nodes), 41 tools |
| Extraction call | 333,184 cached input / 468

uncached input / 9,954 output tokens |
| Extraction duration | 47.6 s |
| Structural compile | 365

candidates, 46 retained |
| Checkpoint | 2,243 characters, approximately 1,121 tokens (audit recorde

d 1,076 tokens) |
| Certificate | supports preserved, selection consistent, condensation reconstruct

s — all true; reconstruction error 0 |
| Fallbacks | none |
On the same span, the shipped backend had previously published a 20,011-character summary (approxima
tely 5,131 tokens). The plugin produced 2,243 characters, every item traceable to a verbatim source
,131 tokens). The plugin produced 2,243 characters, every item traceable to a verbatim source quote.
These figures were measured on v0.3.0, before verbatim retention became the default. From v0.5.0 the
published checkpoint also carries the retention block (see Verbatim retention), so its size is larg
er than the checkpoint figure above; the extraction and structural measurements are unchanged.
Method and limitations:
- This is a replay measurement: the most recent recorded compaction span in the session is rebuilt a
nd passed through one `summarize` call, reporting actual usage and output, without publishing anythi

ng. It therefore measures extraction cost and the checkpoint, not publication cost.
- The replays pr
efix matched a provider cache entry (333,184 tokens) because that prefix had been sent by real reque
sts before. Whether the cache is still valid depends on the provider's retention policy; with a cold

cache the call costs approximately one full prompt read.

measurements of this plugin.

| Steady-state prefix-cache hit rate | 99.20% (25 sessions, 3,515 requests) |

## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The numbered steps:
1. Replay the history being compacted, together with the system prompt and tool list, to the model,
and append an instruction that requests JSON: each item carries a kind, a short summary, and a quote

that must appear verbatim in the source.
2. Verify every quote locally. Items that cannot be locate

d, or that were invented, are discarded.
3. Treat the surviving items as degrees of freedom. Shared
source, adjacency and same-kind establish stiffness; the current request acts as the load; exact anc

hors and open loops are pinned as supports.
4. Solve the KKT system and perform static condensation

to obtain the load-bearing set.
5. Produce a certificate: whether supports were eliminated, whether
the selection is self-consistent, and whether the condensation reconstructs the full response. Any f

ailed check prevents publication.
6. Render the result within the checkpoint budget; the `## Next St
ep` section is always anchored (an extracted next-step atom, or a verbatim floor naming the latest r

equest).
7. Append the verbatim retention block: real user requests and recent units copied from the
source, up to `verbatimTokens`, and clamped so the checkpoint still shrinks its source.
Failures degrade step by step: a failed structural compile falls back to local rendering with no mod
el call; a failed local render falls back to the shipped summarizer. A session is never left without
led local render falls back to the shipped summarizer. A session is never left without a checkpoint.
## Known limitations
- Desktop thresholds and retention come from the preset's shipped engine. Manual `/compact` cuts dee

per than automatic compaction (the shipped engine retains 0 for manual compaction).
- When extractio
n cannot produce verifiable quotes, the checkpoint degrades to deterministic rendering; when that ca
nnot shrink the source, the shipped summarizer runs. Quality therefore depends on the model's citati
on discipline. The certificate establishes structural self-consistency, not information-theoretic co

mpleteness.
- The extraction call cannot reuse the live request cache, so `extract` mode costs the s
ame as the shipped backend. `deterministic` mode skips that call. A replay that is byte-identical to

the live request requires request-time information absent from the log; this is not implemented.
-
The hook depends on one specific shipped method. If that method is renamed or moved, the plugin sile
ntly falls back to the shipped summarizer without breaking the session. Check `hook.backendUsesHooke

dSummarize` after upgrades.
- The desktop preset still mounts the shipped tool-result pruner. Measur
ements show it is a net loss, but this plugin does not control that component. Disabling it requires
overriding the preset declaration; the trade-off is discussed in `docs/DESIGN.md`.
## Privacy and security
The plugin contains no telemetry, makes no network requests of its own and writes no state to disk.
The two loopback diagnostic endpoints are intended for local troubleshooting and contain no conversa
tion content; they can be disabled with `statusCommands: false`. See SECURITY.md.
